Rumors have long circulated that Apple is developing a brand-new, all-glass design iPhone model to mark the 20th anniversary of the iPhone next year. However, an analyst at Jefferies believes that device is no longer moving forward.

Wall Street analyst says the major redesign for the 20th anniversary iPhone has been cancelled

Wall Street investment bank Jefferies downgraded Apple's stock rating to "Underperform" today, with analyst Edison Lee arguing that the likely cancellation of the 20th anniversary iPhone's major redesign is a key reason for the move.

The crux of this downgrade lies in suspicions that Apple's all-glass iPhone project has been scrapped. Although reports dating back to 2025 indicated the project was already in development, with rumors suggesting a launch as early as 2027, Apple has never responded to such speculation. However, the company did quietly file a patent application back in 2019 for a "six-sided glass enclosure." Jefferies previously considered an all-glass iPhone plausible, but Lee now believes development work has come to a halt. According to the analyst, supply-chain checks indicate the project was cancelled due to excessively low yield rates. Lee views this decision as "a major setback for driving premium iPhone sales amid rising memory costs." Had the device actually launched in September 2027 to celebrate the iPhone's 20th anniversary, its blended retail price was projected to reach US$2,060 — higher than the average selling price of any previous model. Lee wrote: "More importantly, we believe the original plan was to extend the all-glass design to future iPhone Pro and Pro Max models, further lifting average selling prices and margins." He sees this as a critical defensive strategy at a time when memory prices keep climbing.

Lee also noted that Apple's AI strategy and rising component costs for the iPhone 19 Pro are additional reasons behind the stock downgrade.

From Lee's report, it is impossible to determine whether he believes the entire redesign project has been shelved, or only certain design elements have been cancelled.

Top comment posted by Currentinterest

These analysts have been wrong about Apple's future plans many times before. The 'all-glass' label may never have accurately reflected the design Apple intended to deliver. Whatever its final specifications, the 20th anniversary handset will be distinctive and highly sought after.

For example, speculation has persisted that Apple may not be able to completely remove the Dynamic Island cutout next year. That would make an 'all-glass' screen impossible. But the rumored four-sided curved design could still debut.

Either way, if Apple's 20th anniversary iPhone redesign has indeed been cancelled, expect other credible sources to corroborate the news in the short term.
